title: Table S1. Inter-reviewer classification agreement in RSv1
note: Primary human analysis: Main 11-50 for each pair, records rated analysable by both reviewers, jointly retained leaf nodes, and post-L1-reassessment labels. Detailed classification comprises 19 HFACS categories plus patient condition (CoP), OTHER, and INAPPROPRIATE. The five-category layer and binary analyses combine the three non-HFACS categories. Counts are the observations entering each classification analysis. Observed agreement is a proportion, not a percentage. Confidence intervals use 2,000 record-cluster bootstrap replicates.

title: Table S2. AI classification agreement with adjudicated RSv1
note: The final evaluation set contained 50 records; 37 were analysable under the adjudicated RSv1 reference and contributed 306 leaf nodes. AI labels were compared with the adjudicated reference. Detailed classification comprises 19 HFACS categories and one combined non-HFACS category (20 categories in total), unlike the 22-category human analysis in Table S1. The selected GPT configuration was primary; Kimi received the unchanged prompt as a secondary evaluation. Confidence intervals use 5,000 record-cluster bootstrap replicates. Pair-stratified resampling was not used in this final RSv1 analysis.

note: All rows use records rated analysable by both reviewers and jointly retained nodes. The first row repeats the primary 22-category analysis as the comparison anchor. Main 1-50 adds the earlier records; non-top nodes include intermediate nodes as well as leaves. Before/after L1 reassessment refers to saved reviewer coding versions, not different patients. The eight 22-category rows enumerate all available combinations of record range, node scope, and coding version. The last two rows show alternative grouping of non-HFACS categories; five-category layer and binary results are in Table S1. Blank classification labels were excluded from classification estimates and preserved in the source dataset. Counts and intervals are taken from the existing analysis, with 2,000 record-cluster bootstrap replicates. These are sensitivity analyses, not additional independent validation cohorts.
